items.title: Second wave of hacks turns up supermarket freezers across Europe
items.why: Attackers reached internet-exposed refrigeration controllers on November 2 and set freezers to about 50°C in more than 50 Belgian stores plus shops in five other countries, spoiling stock. Many units were older models that no longer get updates.
items.action: List building controllers you own (HVAC, fridges, alarms, cameras), take any reachable from the internet offline or behind a VPN, and replace unsupported units.

items.title: Password manager mSecure tells all users to change their stored passwords
items.why: Maker mSeven Software emailed customers on November 3 about suspicious activity tied to the app and urged them to protect everything stored in it. It has not said what was accessed or whether vaults were exposed.
items.action: If anyone on your team uses mSecure, change the passwords it holds starting with banking and email, reset two-factor and passkeys, and consider moving to another manager.

items.title: CISA confirms attacks on the WordPress core update flaw fixed in 7.1.4
items.why: CISA added the WordPress core flaw that lets attackers run code during the brief window a site is updating to its exploited list on November 3. Versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 are affected; fixes cover every supported branch.
items.action: Check each WordPress site's version on the Updates screen, update to 7.1.4 or your branch's fixed release, and confirm agency- or host-managed sites were updated too.

items.title: Brazil's largest crypto exchange halts withdrawals after about $46 million drained
items.why: Mercado Bitcoin, with about 4.5 million customers, froze deposits and withdrawals after a cyberattack on November 2, days after the Binance theft. It says customers were not harmed; outside analysts say some customer wallets were emptied.
items.action: Keep business crypto in wallets you control or spread it across providers, require hardware-key sign-in on exchange accounts, and set withdrawal address allowlists.

items.title: Google takes down a 1.3 million-device botnet built into cheap Android TV boxes
items.why: Google says maker Videostrong deliberately shipped the x.cpe backdoor on set-top boxes, signage players and similar devices, including MECOOL-branded ones, and sold access for ad fraud and proxies. The backdoor survives restarts.
items.action: Find off-brand Android TV boxes and signage players on your network, check them against Synthient's model list, replace matches, and keep smart devices on a guest network.

items.title: Attackers drain hot wallets on older BTCPay Server installs
items.why: BTCPay Server says thieves are emptying Bitcoin and Litecoin hot wallets on merchant servers, with reports since November 1. Version 2.4.1 and earlier are at risk; the latest release, 2.4.7, has no credible drain reports.
items.action: If you take crypto through BTCPay, update to 2.4.7; on 2.4.1 or older, move to a fresh server and new wallet, and keep only operating funds in the hot wallet.
